analysis.title: Welcome to the new normal
key_insights: The S&P 500 fell on a day when more than 80% of its stocks rose, which the note says has not happened in nearly 40 years.
Single-stock volatility relative to the index is approaching extraordinary levels while correlations between S&P 500 stocks have collapsed, so the index tells little about moves underneath.
Materials, Industrials and Communication Services show the biggest dispersion. Staples and Utilities are relatively calm. Single-stock volatility is elevated across almost every sector.

Equal-weight equities have started outperforming as the Magnificent Seven stumble. With mutual fund year-end approaching, the open question is whether portfolio managers keep defending yesterday's winners or rotate into the rest of the market.

Hedge-fund de-grossing since June has reached 8%, the largest sustained reduction on record. Net leverage is back at 51%, but recent buying has been driven largely by short covering rather than conviction buying (Morgan Stanley Prime Brokerage).

Europe's STOXX 600 is about 3% below its highs, but cyclicals have underperformed defensives by 13% and price momentum has unwound 14% since June. Morgan Stanley sees an increasingly attractive setup for a reversal, particularly in Semiconductors, Hardware and Banks.

Morgan Stanley's Mike Wilson believes the correction is entering its final stages. Semiconductors could still fall another 10-15% before finding support around mid-November. His year-end S&P 500 target remains 8,000.

Prediction markets assign a 66% probability to a Democratic sweep in the midterms, per Morgan Stanley's election dashboard. The bank flags NC-03, FL-07, FL-13 and VA-05 as races to watch for signs of a broader Democratic wave.

Luxury hotels are 2% of global hotel properties but generate 15% of room revenue. Morgan Stanley expects the five largest global hoteliers to deliver about 20% annual EPS growth through 2028, versus 10% for luxury goods companies.
